The PSI of R.M.C.Yard Police Station submitted charge sheet against the accused person for the offences punishable under sections 408 and 420 of IPC.
2.

The brief facts of the prosecution case is as follows:-
The case of the prosecution is that the complainant had running the business in the name and style as Shabari Enterprises situated at 93/B, 3rd Main Road,
Goraguntepalya, Yeshavanthapura Industrial Suburb, Bengaluru.
The accused was joined a complainant company as a Sales Executive on 29.08.2016.

In the year 2017 the accused generated the grocery bills in the name of CW-3 to CW-22 from the complainant company and did not supply the grocery items to them and sold the said grocery items to some one for Rs.7,28,988/- and misappropriated the said amount for his personal use and thereby the accused person has committed the criminal breach of trust and cheated the complainant and committed the above offences.

After completion of the investigation the PSI of R.M.C. Yard Police Station has filed the C.C.No.25800/2019 charge sheet against the accused person for the offences punishable under sections 408 and 420 of IPC.
3.
Thereafter, the complainant has lodged the complaint in R.M.C. Yard Police station.
In turn they have registered the case under Crime No.0029/2018.

After hearing the parties and on perusal of records, the following points arose for my consideration.

1. Whether the prosecution proves beyond all reasonable doubt that the complainant had running the business in the name and style as Shabari Enterprises situated at 93/B, 3rd Main Road,
Goraguntepalya, Yeshavanthapura Industrial Suburb, Bengaluru.
The accused was joined a complainant company as a Sales Executive on 29.08.2016.

In the year 2017 the C.C.No.25800/2019 accused generated the grocery bills in the name of CW-3 to CW-22 from the complainant company and did not supply the grocery items to them and sold the said grocery items to some one for Rs.7,28,988/- and misappropriated the said amount for his personal use and thereby the accused person has committed the offence punishable under section 408 of IPC?
2. Whether the prosecution proves beyond all reasonable doubt that the above said date, place and time that in the year 2017 the accused generated the grocery bills in the name of CW-3 to CW-22 from the complainant company and did not supply the grocery items to them and sold the said grocery items to some one for Rs.7,28,988/- and cheated the complainant company and thereby the C.C.No.25800/2019 accused person committed the offence punishable under section 420 of IPC?
3.
What order?

8. Heard the arguments and perused the materials available on records.
9.
My findings to the above points are as follows:
POINT No.1 : In the NEGATIVE.

REASONS 10. Point Nos.1 and 2: These above points are inter- linked with each others and required similar type of appreciation of evidence, Hence, they are taken together for common discussion.

11. In support of its case, the prosecution has examined two witnesses, the PW-1 is the eye witnesses,
and PW-2 is the complainant and got marked three documents as Ex.P-1 to C.C.No.25800/2019 Ex.P-3 i.e., Ex.P-1 is the statement of PW-1,
Ex.P-2 is the complaint dated 27.01.2018 and Ex.P-3 is the mahazar.

12. The case of the prosecution is that the complainant had running the business in the name and style as Shabari Enterprises situated at 93/B, 3rd Main Road, Goraguntepalya, Yeshavanthapura Industrial Suburb, Bengaluru.
The accused was joined a complainant company as a Sales Executive on 29.08.2016.

In the year 2017 the accused generated the grocery bills in the name of CW-3 to CW-22 from the complainant company and did not supply the grocery items to them and sold the said grocery items to some one for Rs.7,28,988/- and misappropriated the said amount for his personal use and thereby the accused person has committed the criminal breach of trust and cheated the complainant and committed the above offences.

After completion of the investigation the PSI of R.M.C.Yard Police Station has filed the charge sheet against the accused person for the offences punishable under sections 408 and 420 of IPC.
13.
In the instant case the PW-1 and 2 have turned hostile to the prosecution case and not supported to the C.C.No.25800/2019 prosecution case.
During the course of cross examination by the learned Sr. APP nothing has been elicited from his mouth.
14. In this case, the prosecution has failed to elicit anything favorable to it to prove the allegations against the accused person under sections 408 and 420 of IPC.
When these being the facts, I am of the opinion that in total the prosecution has failed to bring home the guilt of the accused person beyond all reasonable doubt.
In view of the same, this court hold Point Nos.1 and 2 in the Negative.
15. Point No.3:
For the reasons stated and finding given to point Nos.1 and 2, the following is made.
ORDER The accused person is not found guilty for the offences punishable under section 408 and 420 of IPC.
Acting under section 248(1) of Code of Criminal Procedure the accused person is hereby acquitted for the offences punishable under section 408 and 420 of IPC.
